analista-artificiale.deck: One platform, one US$300 entry, several claims that do not survive contact with its own fine print.
analista-artificiale.depositMethods: Debit/credit cards, PayPal, Skrill, bank transfer
intro: Platform reviews usually answer one question: is it safe? With Analista Artificiale, the better first question is what the platform own pages concede, because they concede quite a lot.
The desk combines AI signals with manual control. Newcomers can start on the practice account, fund US$300 when ready, and trade 9 assets through the partner broker.
The checks below follow the platform published pages in order - what it claims, what the fine print says, and where the two diverge. The verdict is a summary of those checks, nothing more.
whatItClaims: Withdrawals processed in under a day, per the page.
No prior trading experience required.
AI and algorithmic market analysis producing signals and suggested entries.
Automatic or manual execution, with a browser-based platform.
No platform fees - broker spreads and overnight charges still apply.
whatWeChecked: The payout promise: within-a-day wording without processing detail.
The broker relationship: which partner desk executes orders.
The asset list: how many pairs are actually offered.
The registration flow: what personal details the form collects.
The risk disclosure: where the capital-at-risk wording sits.
The security claims: encryption and account protection statements.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Enter your name, email, phone and country, then confirm through the emailed link.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Send the US$300 starting deposit through one of the accepted methods.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Set your preferences, select automatic or manual execution, and run the practice account first.

pros: A browser dashboard - nothing to install.
cons: The demo claim buried in the signup flow.
Performance examples without dates or proof.
Asset list that shifts between pages.
The headline fee claim and the real cost disagree.
redFlags: The fee that is not a fee: spreads embedded in every trade.
Restriction lists that name different countries.
Payout promises with no processing detail.

faqs.a: 9 crypto assets through broker partners, per the published pages. The list varies between sections, so check the dashboard after signup.
Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.
The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.
The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.

bottomLine: The service behind the marketing looks functional, and a careful user can use it without stepping on the fine print.
The scorecard settles at 4.5. That is a cautious pass - proceed with the demo first, the minimum deposit second, and treat every payout figure as unproven until you see it yourself.
